overview: Diabetes is a chronic disease that occurs either when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces. Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood glucose. Hyperglycaemia, also called raised blood glucose or raised blood sugar, is a common effect of uncontrolled diabetes and over time leads to serious damage to many of the body's systems, especially the nerves and blood vessels. Diabetes can be treated and its consequences avoided or delayed with diet, physical activity, medication and regular screening and treatment for complications.
symptoms: needing to urinate more often than usual
treatment: regular screening and treatment for complications
prevention: reaching and keeping a healthy body weight
eating a healthy diet and avoiding sugar and saturated fat
key_facts: Diabetes caused over 2 million deaths in 2021
Around 11% of cardiovascular deaths were caused by high blood glucose
14% of adults aged 18 years and older were living with diabetes in 2022
